title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
title_zh: APEX：用于极致压缩的异步前缀去噪技术

paragraphs.en: APEX 是一种用于极致压缩的异步前缀去噪技术，改善了潜在空间压缩带来的重建与生成困境。 Fewer latent tokens promise cheaper diffusion. Yet aggressive latent compression creates a reconstruction-generation dilemma: adding channels improves reconstruction but makes generation harder. We introduce APEX, short for Asynchronous Prefix denoising for EXtreme compression, which pairs a hierarchical latent space with asynchronous denoising over channel groups. Our autoencoder orders channel prefixes from structure to detail, while one shared denoiser generates them at staggered local times without adding tokens. On ImageNet-512, APEX outperforms existing methods at every evaluated channel count under 64x and 128x compression. At matched training and guided sampling compute, it also outperforms a 256-token model at every evaluated budget, with larger gains at lower compute. Code is available at https://daviddinkevich.github.io/APEX.
paragraphs.zh: APEX 是一种用于极致压缩的异步前缀去噪技术，它改善了潜在空间压缩所带来的重建与生成困境。更少的潜在标记意味着更低的扩散成本。 然而，激进的潜在压缩会引发重建与生成之间的困境：增加通道能提升重建效果，却会使生成变得更加困难。 我们提出了 APEX（即“用于极致压缩的异步前缀去噪”），它将分层潜在空间与针对通道组的异步去噪相结合。 我们的自动编码器按从结构到细节的顺序排列通道前缀，同时一个共享的去噪器无需增加标记，即可在不同局部时间依次生成这些前缀。 在 ImageNet-512 数据集上，当压缩倍率低于 64x 和 128x 时，APEX 在所有评估的通道数量上都优于现有方法。 在训练和引导采样计算量匹配的情况下，它在所有评估的预算水平上也优于 256 标记模型，尤其是在较低计算量下优势更为显著。 代码可在 https://daviddinkevich.github.io/APEX 获取。
